Commentary.Commentary: The conditions did favour the home team this morning and their pacers took no time in picking up the remaining wickets. The score is still a good one and the conditions are still overcast. It is going to be a testing period for the English openers and they would hope to get through this safely. India, on the other hand, will try their best to get some quick wickets before Lunch. Stay tuned.

The England bowling had contrasting stories. They were brilliant when the conditions overhead were cloudy, the first session of Day 1 was an example as Chris Woakes managed to take three quick wickets. However, as the sun came out, the swing was not visible and the bowlers could not produce the same magic. Adil Rashid was expected to deliver but he was not up to the mark, although he bagged the prized scalp of Virat Kohli.

India though will still be happy with their overall batting performance. First, it was Dhawan and Rahul who got them off to a solid start but then three quick wickets had put them on the back foot. Post that, Virat Kohli along with the vice-captain, Ajinkya Rahane, who was in desperate need of runs, came to the fore. The pair added 159 which set the foundation for a big first innings total. The lower order added handy runs but failed to take the total past the 350-run mark.

Boom, boom, boom, that is how England have gone about their business this morning. 22 runs, that's all India have managed to add to their overnight total. Once again it is the duo of Broad and Anderson who have made use of the bowling-friendly conditions and bundled out the remaining wickets in no time.

OUT! Bowled 'em! It's all over for India. England have wrapped up the Indian innings earlier than they would have expected. Anderson fires this outswinger on a length and attacking the stumps. Bumrah tries to block it from the crease. But the slight away movement beats the outside edge of his bat and the ball shatters the stumps. INDIA ALL OUT FOR 329!
Jasprit Bumrah is the next batsman in.

OUT! And the aggressive tactics have not worked for Shami here. Anderson keeps it on a length on middle and off. Shaping away after landing. Shami, as he tried earlier in the over, goes for a wild swing. The ball moves away slightly on hitting the deck and he gets a top edge. The ball flies high in the air and Stuart Broad at mid on takes the skier safely.
Full and attacking the stumps, Shami defends well off the front foot.
Better from Shami. Anderson keeps it on a length around the off stump. Shami gets behind the line of the ball and blocks it out.

Shami swinging with all his might here. Anderson keeps it full just outside off, there is good away shape to the ball. Shami gives it a big swing and misses the ball completely. Is this India's tactics to go after the bowling?

A peach to end it! Broad has his tail up here. He is really making the ball talk. On a length around off, this time he gets the ball to move away. Ishant is squared up as he tries to defend and the ball goes past the outside edge.

What a shot to get off the mark! Full and outside off, Shami slaps it through covers, not off the middle but enough to get three. Handy runs are these for India. They would take every one of them with open arms.
Mohammed Shami walks in to bat.

OUT! KABOOM! What an absolute beauty! That has swung in like a banana and very late. Almost similar to the delivery Broad got Pujara with in the last Test. Unplayable. Pujara had no answers and now Ashwin too has none. Broad comes running in and bowls it full outside off, it comes back in very late. Ashwin has his front foot planted across but then seeing the ball tail back in, he tries to flick. He misses, the ball hits his pads and then uproots the middle pole. Broad gets his second this morning and England are now into the tail which they would want to clean up as quickly as possible.
On the shorter side, Ashwin defends it onto the ground.

An appeal but not given! On a length around off, it pitches and then moves away. Ashwin tries to flick but misses to get hit on the thigh pad. Broad appeals but the umpire shakes his head. The impact and the height were the issues there.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

EDGED BUT DROPPED! Pope drops a sharp chance. Excellent delivery to end the over. Another outswinger, once again it is fuller than the previous deliveries. Ashwin is only half forward as he tries to defend it. The ball takes the outside edge and goes low and quickly towards fourth slip. The man there dives and gets a hand to it but fails to hang on. The ball rolls towards short third man and the batsmen take a run.
Off the mark is Ishant now! He taps this ball towards covers and sprints to the other end.

Good cricket here! Another very good delivery which was equally well played. Anderson bowls it on a back of a length around off, this one moves away late. Ishant first thinks of playing at it but then at the last moment bails out.
Nicely played! On the shorter side and on off, Ashwin goes back and punches it towards covers for a quick run.
Shortens his length this time and bowls it on off, Ashwin easily blocks it out.
BEATEN! Loose, very loose by Ashwin there. A sucker ball outside off, swinging away. Ashwin goes after it with no foot movement. Luckily for him the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Full and swinging in again. This time a bit too much of swing though. Ishant tries to get bat on ball but the inward movement beats his bat and the ball hits his pads. Going down leg though.
Keeps it full on the off stump. The inswing makes the ball swirl into Ishant, who does well to get behind the line of the ball and block it out.
Ishant Sharma walks in next. He has been promoted up the order, batted at no. 11 in the last game and no. 10 in the first Test.

OUT! Drags it on. And it's the debutant, Pant, who has to take the long walk back. Broad this time keeps it a bit fuller outside off. He gets it to swing away from Pant after pitching. The southpaw, who was showing good patience and grit until now, goes for an extravagant drive through the covers. He reaches out a bit, away from his body with zero footwork. As a result, the ball takes the inside edge and crashes into the stumps. Pant looks dejected. Broad gives him a send-off. Hmm...
This is the first indication of the ball keeping low. He lands it on the 6th stump line again. Pant leaves.
Similar delivery. Keeps it on a length outside off, Pants watchfully lets it go.
Well, a halt in play as Broad has some issue with his shoe. Trevor Bayliss in the dressing room is seen signalling to send in a replacement.
Starts the over with a fuller length delivery outside off. The ball moves away after pitching. But the line is a bit too wide to entice Pant into a shot. He lets it go behind.

EDGED BUT FOUR! Anderson this time bowls it fuller, meaning Ashwin can't play it that late. The batter pokes at it with soft hands. The ball takes the outside edge and goes through the slip cordon for the second boundary of the over. So runs coming thick and fast for India this morning and they have crossed the 320-run mark.
No swing this time as it is a touch shorter on off, Ashwin off the back foot punches it to mid off.

FOUR! Excellent by Ashwin! He is playing the ball very late, which is working in his favour. Another good delivery by Anderson, on off, shapes away. Ashwin stays rooted to his crease, lets the ball come to him and then guides it through backward point for a boundary. His second.
Again a little too wide outside off, Ashwin lets it go through to the keeper.
Perfect! This time he angles it on off and then gets it to move away. Ashwin though plays it really late as he defends it to point. Good cricket all around.
On a length around off, shapes away from the batsman. Ashwin plays inside the line and lets it go to the keeper. Anderson needs to be bowling it a touch straighter.
Pant tries to flick this length ball angling into him, again misses and JB behind dives to his right to collect it. End of a quite wayward over by Broad, failing to control his line.
Gets his line wrong this time and stray it down the leg side. Pant tries to tuck it around but does not get bat on it.
Wider and fuller outside off, Pant does not fiddle with it.
Pant gets right behind the line of this full length delivery on the stumps and defends solidly.
Keeps it on a length outside off, Pant lets it go.

Broad comes from round the wicket, a length ball angled into Pant, who gets inside the line of the ball and tries to tuck it around. The ball hits his thigh pad and runs down fine on the leg side. Adil Rashid on deep fine leg boundary does well to dive and stop two runs for his team.
On the pads, Pant tucks it away to fine leg and retains strike.
Nearly drags it on! A good bumper outside off, Pant tries to drag his pull but gets a bottom edge onto his boot.
Another good side of Pant. He is also leaving the ball really well, not getting tempted and he does that here.
Very good by the youngster. Not only is he standing outside the crease but he is also shuffling across, covering the swing, getting right behind the delivery and blocking it.
Full and outside off, swinging away further. Pant shoulders arms to it.
Good length on off, Pant covers the swing by moving across and defends it.
James Anderson will bowl from the other end.

FOUR! What just happened there? Did Buttler not sight the ball or he could just not react? Will have to wait for a replay to find out as Ashwin gets off the mark with a boundary. Not in a convincing manner though. Broad bowls it on a back of a length outside off, Ashwin goes after it with no foot movement, a needless shot to be honest. The ball takes a thick outside edge and goes over Buttler at second slip, who just could not get up in time. A boundary at third man results. End of a good over for India, they have started on a positive note.
Attacks the stumps and this one stays a touch low. Ashwin gets his bat down in time and hits it towards mid on.
Once again Broad bowls it outside off, the batsman need not play at those. It swings in after passing the batsman. JB does really well behind the stumps to collect it.

Sir Ian Botham (on air) feels that the pitch will get quicker today and it was a bit tacky yesterday. David Bumble adds to it that usually Day 2 is the best day to bat as the pitch becomes easy-paced.
Better from Broad! Bowls it straighter this time but no movement available. Pant tucks it with the angle through square leg and gets to the other end. First run today.
Swing again but the line is a little too wide outside off, moves away further and Pant makes another leave.

Some movement first up, expected, looking at the conditions overhead. Broad comes running in and lands it on a length around off, it pitches and then moves away. Pant watchfully lets it go through to the keeper.

So after the delay we are all set for the action to begin now. The Indian batsmen, Ravichandran Ashwin and Rishabh Pant walk out to the middle. The latter will be on strike and he will face Stuart Broad. Three slips in place. Here we go...
UPDATE 1107 local - Well, we will have to wait a little more longer as now play will resume at 1130 local. A few wet areas out there that the groundsmen are trying to dry. Stay tuned.

The former English skipper, Alastair Cook, is up for a chat with Michael Atherton. On catching in the slips, he replies it's more comfortable fielding in the slip cordon with those you have been doing it for long. Adds further that their slip catching has not been great lately. Mentions they have been working on the type of catch he took yesterday and he is delighted it stuck. Admits that Trent Bridge has not been his favourite ground but he hopes his fortune will change. Reckons playing spin now is much more difficult than it was earlier due to the use of the DRS. Reminds that earlier the batsmen used to take a long stride forward with the bat hiding behind the pads but now they have to play more with the willow. Feels that the dangerous ball is the one which skids on with the arm. Ends by saying that the way they bat in the first innings will be very crucial.
Good news folks! The covers seem to be coming off and the news coming in is, play will get underway at 1115 local, weather permitting that is.

England's pacers, on the other hand, will be keen on utilizing the pacer-friendly morning conditions and keep the visitors in check. Let us hope we get another day of exciting cricket. For now, though, there is a steady DRIZZLE and the COVERS are on the pitch. There is still time for play to start so let us hope it clears by then and we get underway soon.

Hello and welcome to the coverage of Day 2 of the third Test between England and India. With the pendulum of momentum swinging from one team to the other throughout Day 1, both teams are looking to get a strong hold on this match. The first session will be crucial as India's primary  target will be to cross 350. However, if Pant and Ashwin bat to their potential, the visitors could even get near 400 or even surpass it.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

It's been a superb day of Test cricket. India started well but then England shot back courtesy Chris Woakes. Then, the tourists recovered from the quick blows owing to the 159-run stand between Kohli and Rahane. Both the batsmen however were very unlucky not to get their centuries. After going wicket-less for the entire afternoon session, the hosts managed to pick three more in the evening session to end the day's play on level terms. The wicket looks good for batting, with not a lot of assistance for the bowlers. Let us hope we are up for a similar day of cricket on Day 2. Do join us then. Take care and goodbye!

India do not have a lot of batting to come but they would hope for Pant along with the remaining batters to contribute and cross the 350-run mark. The hosts, on the other hand, will look to bundle out the remaining wickets quickly and then try and bat well.

Earlier in the day, after being put into bat, Rahul and Dhawan got India off to a solid start. Woakes then brought the hosts back into the game with three quick wickets. Kohli and Rahane then rose to the occasion and built a huge partnership to put India on the front foot. But wickets at crucial intervals helped the home side hang around in the game.

Virat Kohli looked destined for another ton but once again he fell prey to the spin of Rashid. England at that moment would have sniffed a chance to run through the remaining wickets but the debutant, Pant, showed no signs of nerves. He played his shots and his partnership with Hardik saw India cross the 300-run mark for the first time in this series. They were really batting well and it seemed like the tourists would end the day on top but Anderson's 100th Test scalp against India at the very end means things, for now, stand even-stevens.

What an attritional day of cricket! Both sides, I believe, will be happy heading into the dugout. More so England, who have fought back really well in the last session by picking up three vital wickets. Kohli and Rahane were cruising along after the Tea break. The two added 159 before the latter was dismissed 19 short of a ton. Kohli then, along with Pandya, continued as the pair added another handy partnership.

OUT! A wicket right at the fag end. This is Anderson's 100th Test wicket against India. What a champion bowler. Pandya had to see off just that one more ball - but fails to do so. Jimmy continues to probe away in the corridor of uncertainty but this was a ball which perhaps Hardik could have left. But that compulsive 'have-to-put-bat-to-ball' mindset in him forces the all-rounder to come forward and have a tame push. There is some extra bounce on the ball and it also seams away a bit after hitting the deck. That movement allows the ball to take the outside edge. It flies to second slip, where Buttler takes his second catch of the innings. Pandya walks back like a man furious with the whole world. Throughout the over and also the one before, he was asking the umpires - 'How many balls left? How many balls left?' Well, that particular eagerness to head back to the dressing room might have cost him his wicket. THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 1!
In-swinging yorker, well thought out by Anderson. Pandya is up to the task as he digs it out in the nick of time.
Pandya shows the full face of the bat and defends this length ball off the back foot.
Short of a length ball, it pitches and gets extra bounce off the deck. Also seams away after pitching. Pandya lunges forward and is beaten.
Well left. Anderson angles this into Pandya from just outside off. There is some good away shape and Pandya has nothing to do with it.
Length ball on the off pole, defended solidly by Pandya.
Almost! On a length around off, this one pitches and then skids through. Pant tries to leave it but gets an inside edge which bounces just in front of the stumps.
Fuller in length on off, Rishabh defends it towards point.
On a length around off, Pant guides it to point.
A little too wide outside off, Pant makes a leave.
Excellent comeback delivery! Short of a length and on off, this one pitches and straightens. Pant plays inside the line and the ball whizzes past the outside edge.

FOUR! Lovely! This young lad is just showing he belongs at the highest level. Yes, it is a half-volley but it still has to be put away and Pant does it with swag. He smashes it through covers and the ball races away.
Outside off, Pandya pokes at it and gets beaten.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Wide outside off, the batsman need not play at those.
On off, the batsman blocks it out.
On the stumps, kept out.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Ends this testing over with a beauty again. Broad keeps this on a length just outside off. The ball skids through and Pant plays inside the line of the ball. Gets beaten.

Beaten again! Broad looking threatening here. An important phase for both the teams. Pant looks to block this length ball just outside off, however, it nips away after pitching but luckily for Pant it just misses his outside edge.
Pant has nothing to do with this fuller ball outside off.

FOUR! Lovely Shot! And that's 300 up for India with a lovely clip off his pads. Broad angles this in on a length, Pant turns it around in the gap at mid wicket. The timing takes the ball across the fence.

Beats the bat! Much better from Broad as he fires this one from an angle into the batsman. Pant goes towards the ball, but it goes away on pitching. The slight movement away is enough to beat the tentative poke. Pant needs to focus and try and stay till the end.
Broad comes round the wicket. Keeps it just behind the length, but the line is too wide of the off stump. Pant watches it go through.
Back of a length on off, Pandya plays it with soft hands towards gully.

FOUR! Streaky! India won't mind though. On a length and it shapes away. Pandya puts in a big stride and tries to block. The ball takes the outside edge and goes down to the third man fence. One short of 300 now India.
Nice shape! The outswinger from off stump. Pandya first tries to defend but then pulls his bat out.
Fullish and on off, Pant strokes it well through covers, not right off the middle but gets a run for it.
Closer to the off pole this time, Pant gets right behind the line of the delivery and blocks it out.
Good length delivery outside off, Pant does not fiddle with it.
Broad keeps it wide outside off but cannot entice Pandya to chase it.
Pandya goes on the back foot to this length ball on off and defends it with a straight bat.

DROPPED! Jennings is the culprit, he has dropped a sitter. A jaffa from Broad. He lands it on a length just outside off. This one though pitches and climbs with some movement into Pandya. He tries to defend but the ball but it brushes his gloves, hits his shoulder and lobs in the air towards gully. Keaton Jennings there dives to his right, gets two hands to it but spills it. Stuart Broad cannot believe it. Pandya gets a life, can he capitalize on it?
Dishes it outside off, Pandya leaves.
Some away movement for Broad. Keeps it on a length outside off. Pandya shoulder his arms to it.
Broad starts with a short and wide delivery outside off. Pandya does not fiddle with it and lets it go.
Stuart Broad to share the second new ball with Anderson.
Outside off again, Pant makes his third leave in a row. Good temperament shown by the southpaw.
Another ball way outside off, Anderson trying to play with the youngsters patience. However, Pant does not play at it.
Well left! On a length outside off, Pant plants his front foot forward and lets it be.
Classy! On the pads, Pant nonchalantly flicks it through backward sqaure leg and takes two. The youngster looks really confident out there.
Drags his length back on middle, Pant defends it onto the ground.
Some issues with the landing area as the groundsmen has come out with the shovel.
Goes full straightaway and gets some shape into the batsman. Pant goes for the drive but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
The second new ball is now available and it has been taken immediately. Also the spearhead of the English bowling attack, Anderson, comes back into the attack.
Another short ball outside off, Pant hits it towards sweeper cover and retains strike.
Quicker and shorter outside off, Pandya slaps it through cover for a run.
Flighted ball on off, Pandya lunges and strokes it to mid off.
Loopy ball on off, Pandya strokes it to covers.
Extra bounce! Quicker on middle, this one picthes and shoots off the surface. Pandya does well to defend it onto the ground.
Floats it up outside off, Pandya lets it be.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Another bouncer, Pandya ducks under it.
Tucks it with the angle towards mid-wicket for a run.
Down the leg side, Pant misses the flick and Jonny behind the stumps fumbles.
A yorker the last ball, now bowls a bumper, aimed at the rib cage of the batsman. Pant lets it go through to the keeper.
Goes for the inswinging yorker but Pant gets his bat down in time and jams it out.
Again on the pads. He flicks it through the on side and keeps the strike.
A low full toss on middle, Pant works it to the mid-wicket region. A brace results.
Googly on middle, Pant taps it to the off side for nothing.
Defended off the front foot by Pant presenting the full face of the bat.

SIX! Oh my, my! Are you kidding me right now? Hot blood of youth and Delhi's brashness equals to Rishabh Pant, isn't it? Well, that's a way to get off the mark in Test cricket. Not even the greatest of great can say that they hit a maximum to get off the mark. He sees the flight on this one and takes a few steps towards the ball. Lofts it over the long on fence for a brutal six to become the first Indian batsman to get his name on the scoreboard in such a style. Let the carnage begin!
Starts his Test career with a drive to covers.
Defends this one to the off side for no run. Out of nowhere, the English crowd has found some voice.
Comes forward to cover his off pole and then gets his bat away from the line.
Again in the same channel from Ben, left alone.
Hardik lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Down the leg side, Pandya looks to flick but misses.
Play and a miss. Hardik looks to play the length ball around off and gets beaten inside the line.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN AT FIRST SLIP! Rashid strikes! No ton for captain Kohli. Contrasting emotions out there as we see the English side and the fans celebrate while Kohli walks back dejected, disgusted and disappointed. Huge, huge wicket with only 14 overs to go and the second new ball around the corner. Rashid bowls a beautifully tossed up delivery, enticing the batsman to go for the drive. Kohli could not stop himself as he tries to caress it through covers. The ball turns and also bounces a touch more. Takes the outside edge and settles into the hands of Stokes. End of a masterful knock by the run machine. He becomes only the third Indian batsmen to get out in the 90s at Trent Bridge. England though will now look to get a few more before Stumps as Rishabh Pant, the debutant, walks out to the middle.
Loopy ball on middle, VK prods forward and keeps it out.
The googly, Kohli picks it and tucks it to mid-wicket.
Slightly shorter and quicker outside off, Kohli goes for the cut but mistimes it to point. He should have put that away. He will disappointed.
Well bowled! This is tossed up on off, Kohli lunges and blocks it out.
Couple! Rashid has been poor till now. He bowls another drag down. Kohli goes back and punches it through covers, there is a fielder in the deep so it is only a brace. Three away now.
On a length in line of the stumps, blocked down the track for no run.

Streaky. Not the shot you'd expect Kohli to play. He comes forward to play the length ball wide of off. It goes off the inside edge towards fine leg. An easy single taken, even though Virat wanted a second.
Down the leg side once again, Kohli looks to flick but misses.
On a length around middle and off, Kohli defends it.
Too straight from Ben going down the leg side. Kohli misses out.
Fuller outside off, pushed to covers for no run.
It's been driven superbly through the covers.
Works it against the turn to the man at mid-wicket.
Flatter outside off, Pandya lets it be.
FOUR! Too short and Pandya puts it away in some style! A half-tacker on middle, Rashid goes back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary.

NOT OUT! He is not right. The noise he might have heard was of the ball hitting the pad. Rashid bowls the googly outside off, this one comes back in after pitching. Hardik with his bat behind the pad tries to leave it as the ball just about goes past the off pole. Ben Stokes is seen appealing but he is the only one doing so. He then walks upto Root and convinces him to go for the review. Root gets convinced as he signals the 'T'. Replays roll in and they show the ball brushes the pad and not the gloves. Also the LBW is being checked which shows the impact to be outside off. England's second review also goes down the drain.

Review time! Well a late review has been taken. Ben Stokes was the man who convinced his skipper. He felt there was an edge there but by the look of things, it seemed like he was the only one who felt so. Let us see if he is right...
Tosses it up on middle, Pandya drives it to mid on.
Not as fuller as the last delivery and hence Kohli makes a leave.
Fuller in length on off, Kohli times it but finds covers.
On the middle stump, Kohli strokes it back towards the bowler. Stokes tries to get a hand to it but is not able to.
A bumper on middle, Kohli gets on top of the bounce and pulls it all along the ground towards deep mid-wicket for another brace. Just a maximum away now from a ton.
Back of a length outside off, Kohli gets on top of the bounce and guides it towards third man for a couple.
Slower ball on middle, Kohli blocks it out.
Ben Stokes is back on.
FOUR! To end the over! Anderson bowls it a touch too full, no swing which means it is too easy for the batsman. He drives it through covers and the ball runs away to the fence.
The inswinger this time, Pandya though reads it and works it to mid-wicket. He thinks of a run but is rightfully sent back. The fielder scores a direct hit at the keeper's end but Pandya is well in.
Lovely delivery! Drags his length back than the previous delivery and then gets it to move away. Pandya first thinks of playing at it but then pulls his bat away.
Fuller again on off, this one shapes away a touch. Hardik tries to drive it down the ground but gets an outside edge to point.
Good length but the line is outside off, left alone.
Goes fuller on middle, Pandya strokes it to mid on.

Drinks! So, after toiling around for a while, England have finally managed to break the dangerous looking 159-run partnership. However, on a sunny day, it will be a difficult task to bowl out the set looking Kohli. They will need some inspirational bowling performance to make further inroads. The last hour of the day's play coming up next, hang around!
Into the 90s now! On the pads, Kohli flicks it through backward square leg and takes a couple.
Fuller in length on off, no inswing this time. Kohli mistimes his drive to mid off.
FOUR BYES! Once again, a harsh call on the keeper as this was way down the leg side. Bairstow tries his best to collect it with a dive but he had no chance.
Again it comes back in from outside off, Kohli plants his front foot forward and keeps it out.
Starts this one from outside off, gets it to come back in late. Kohli tries to drive but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
FOUR! Tickled and tickled fine! Wrong line by Broad, down the leg side and he flicks it to the fine leg fence. Kohli moves onto one run more than a number which is considered unlucky in Australia.
Again way too outside off, left alone. So not such a great over by Anderson, guilty of bowling too far outside off to Pandya.
Wide outside off, tempting the batsman to go for a loose shot. Pandya does not get tempted and lets it through to the keeper.
Shorter in length on middle, the ball sticks in the surface and also stays a touch low. Pandya has all the time in the world to adjust and block it.
Better! Bowled on a length and around off, gets it to straighten. The batsman tries to defend but gets an outside edge to point.
However, they need to make him play. This is bowled outside off, Pandya does not fiddle with it.
Good length outside off, Kohli guides it through point and gives the strike over to Pandya. England won't mind that run as the new man is now on strike.
Outside off, left alone.
Defended off the front foot by Hardik presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Pandya creams the on drive superbly and earns himself a boundary through the wide mid on region. He has been pushed up the order and needs to prove his mantle to cement his spot.
He gets behind the line of this one and defends it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Pushes this one through covers for a run.
Pandya lets the ball go outside his off stump.
A back of a length ball on the pads, Kohli works it to the on side for a run.
Punches this ball through covers and a brace results.
FOUR! How good is that shot? Classy from Kohli. A length ball on off, he punches it off the back through cover-point. A boundary results.
Shortish around off, Kohli cuts it to point for no run.
Virat chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Hardik Pandya walks in next for the visitors. James Anderson also comes in for another spell.

OUT! Spider-Man or Alastair Cook? Well, it's difficult to differentiate right now considering the way ball stuck to his hand. Reaction time - 0.493 seconds. What a catch! Rahane lunges forward to play the length ball outside his off stump but the ball gets the outside edge and goes past Bairstow in a hurry. Cook, at first slip, sees it late perhaps or he wanted his keeper to go for it. However, he still puts his left hand out and the ball just sticks like mine on fries. He stands right up and high-fives his teammates. A wicket against the run of play and India lose Rahane for 81. A 159-run stand has also been broken.
On the pads, flicked through mid-wicket. The batsmen run two courtesy of some good pro-active running.
Wide outside off, punched off the back foot towards covers. The ball goes through the fielder there and a brace results.
Drives the ball to cover off the front foot.
Kohli has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Another full ball around off, driven for no run.
Full on off, driven to mid off for no run.

FOUR! WOW! This has gone to the fence like a tracer bullet. No half measures from Rahane. He gets a length ball with some width on offer. The bat meets the ball with intent and there's no stopping it as it goes through cover-point for another boundary. 17 runs came off this one. It looks all too easy now.
150-run stand is up. What a partnership this has been. Kohli drives it wide of covers and runs a single to bring up the milestone.

FOUR! Kohli is oozing class right now. What a cracker of a shot this is. No flashiness, he just gets to the pitch of the ball and sends it to the long off fence. Partnership is 149 between the duo now.
On the pads, Ajinkya wrists it away to the on side for another easy single.
FOUR! A gentle gift to Rahane from Woakes and he obliges. A short ball on leg, Rahane pulls it fine with a nice swivel. The ball races to the fence. 7 off the first 2.
Full on off, Kohli bottom-hands it through mid-wicket. Three runs taken after Stokes cuts it out.
Gets nicely behind the line of this one and keeps it out to the off side.
On the hips, flicked through square leg for a run.
Too wide outside off to entice Kohli into a shot.
FOUR! Not sure if it was where Kohli intended but he will take the boundary nonetheless. A short ball on middle and leg, Kohli half-pulls it and keeps it down. The ball goes fine and into the fence.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full around off, pushed to covers.
Outside off, left alone.
On middle and off, Kohli moves across and works it to deep backward square leg. Another run ensues.
Rahane swivels to play the shortish ball towards the fine leg fielder. A run taken.
A length ball on middle, defended.
Rahane plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man. No run taken.

Squares him up there. A back of a length ball on middle and off, Rahane looks to flick it through the on side but closes the face of his bat a touch early. It takes the leading edge and goes towards the point region for nothing.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On the off pole, Kohli plays it out.

Tries to hit the pads of Kohli but Virat is up for the task. He gets his bat down in time and times it sweetly off the middle through square leg. Pope in the deep runs to his left, dives and saves two runs for his team.
Goes wide of the crease and angles it on off, Virat lunges and blocks it.
The outswinger but the line is way outside off, Kohli shoulders arms to it.
This one stays a touch low after it lands on off, Kohli does really well to get his bat down in time and keep it out.
Rahane leaves the length ball outside his off stump. Just a boundary off this one. India 210/3.
Full on off, driven to covers.
Another shortish ball, cut to point for no run.

FOUR! Up and over. Easy-peasy for Rahane. A short ball with a lot of width, he cuts it over the infield and into the cover-point fence. Runs are now coming thick and fast. India are  in a commanding position.
A tad shorter, kept out off the back foot for nothing.
Gets behind the line of this one and keeps it out.

Geez! Another screamer from Broad. He is asking some question on a dead-looking pitch. He bowls another bullet just outside off and makes Kohli lunge forward. He fails to connect again as it nips away.
Virat lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Checks his drive again but couldn't get it past the cover fielder.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Goodness me, what a beauty! Broad dishes this one just outside off, it has the natural angle coming back into Kohli who goes forward to defend it. The ball holds its line and whizzes past the edge. A nervy moment!
On a length on off from Broad, defended.
Works this one to the on side and changes strike. A good over for the visitors.
FOUR! Cheeky from Cheeku. A shortish ball with some width on offer. Kohli opens the face of the bat and gets it past third slip for a boundary.
Outside off, left alone by Kohli.
Full on off, driven to covers for no run.

Ooh! Refrain from playing such shots, Virat Kohli. A length ball from Woakes wide outside off, it's full and therefore Kohli goes for the cover drive. But did not get the timing he wanted on it and as a result, it goes aerially there.
Defended off the back foot by Rahane. They pick up a single.
Cuts the length ball through cover-point and keeps the strike for the next over.
Full on off, driven back to the bowler.
Ajinkya lets the ball go outside his off stump.
FOUR! Edged but safe. A length ball around off, Rahane pokes at it and gets a thickish outside edge. The ball goes through the slip cordon and to the boundary.
Kohli defends it from within the crease. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Beautifully timed drive straight to covers.

Dropped! Fiercely cut by Rahane and Anderson is equally up to it. A short ball this which Rahane cuts off the back foot. The ball goes towards the fielder at point. Anderson there jumps to perfection and puts his hand to almost pull off a blinder. The ball, however, hits his hand and drops to his right. The fielder next to him couldn't get to it either. No harm done in the end but a difficult chance goes down but also a boundary saved.
Full, no swing or seam, Rahane lets it be.
Comes back in this time. Rahane works it to point for nothing.
Wide outside off stump, Ajinkya leaves it alone.
Similar delivery from Chris. Rahane is happy to defend it.
Clever! A back of a length ball on off, Kohli taps it to the off side and takes a quick single.
Chris Woakes to bowl from the other end.
Broad bowls a length ball outside off and couldn't entice Rahane with a shot.
Length ball just outside, blocked.
Defended off the front foot by Rahane presenting the full face of the bat.
Gets behind the line of the ball and keeps it out.
Outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Bang! Gloves are off, punches are being thrown now. Rahane looking good and settled. He gets a ball, a tad too full and he checks his drive. The timing is sublime and the ball races to the cover fence in a jiffy. What a start to the session!
Welcome back. Virat Kohli and Ajinkya Rahane stride out to the middle for the post-tea session. Stuart Broad will bowl the first over after the break. Off we go...
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

The England bowlers gave their all but never looked like dismissing either Kohli or Rahane. Also, once the sun was out, the conditions did not assist them. Rashid was poor when he was brought on, guilty of bowling either too full or too short. They need to come out after the break with a certain plan to break this stand or the two might just take the game away from the hosts. Join us for the all-important final session in some time.

An excellent session for India, a wicket-less one, courtesy the captain and the vice-captain who walk off to a standing ovation from the dressing room and the crowd. These two joined forces after the break and made batting look really easy. They got their eye in and then started milking the bowlers. Both have got a half century each and have stitched a 107-run stand so far, thereby putting India on the front foot. The tourists would hope for them to continue with the good work and convert this into a massive partnership.
Back of a length on off, Kohli defends it out. Tea on day 1!
FOUR BYES! Harsh on the keeper, that! Down the leg side, it moves away further. Bairstow dives full stretch to his left, gets a glove to it but can't stop it cleanly. It crosses the fine leg fence.
On the pads, Rahane works it down to fine leg and gets to the other end.
Bowls the bumper on middle, Rahane evades it.
Good length again on off, Rahane guides it to point.
On the stumps, blocked out.
Shorter of a length, wide outside off, pitches and seams away further, Kohli shoulders arms.
A bit short and a bit wide will not trouble this duo. Rahane goes back to this shortish delivery outside off and tucked it towards the point region for a single.
Pulls the length back a bit and keeps it just back of a length. The ball kicks up on landing. Rahane looks to defend but is hit on the gloves.
The rib-ticklers continue to be fired at the batsmen but it does not seem to trouble them much. Rahane gets under this ball to let it past.
This time Rahane is not sucked into the shot, as he does well to leave the bouncer alone.
Continues with the short ball plan, Rahane goes back and pulls it, gets it from the middle but straight to the square leg fielder.
Goes for the yorker but ends up bowling a low full toss. Rahane hits it back to the bowler who half-stops it and a run is taken.
Hits the length hard on off, Rahane keeps it out.
Good length outside off, Rahane tries to defend it with soft hands but the ball takes the outside edge before rolling towards the man at gully.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman.
On middle, Rahane works it with the angle to mid-wicket.
A back of a length delivery, the fullest ball of the over. Kohli goes back and defends it with a straight bat.
Wide! Too short and too wide, even for a Test match. Given as a wide. Also the 100-run stand comes up courtesy that extra. These two have batted India into a commanding position now.
This tactic seems to  have unsettled the Indian skipper. He goes for a pull again to this bumper outside off. Misses it again and the England players have their hands on their heads.
And the chin music continues, Kohli lets this bouncer go through to Bairstow.
Surely a tactic, almost worked. Short outside off again, Kohli goes for a half-hearted pull but misses the ball by a distance.
Banged in short again. Seems to be a ploy this by England. Kohli ducks under it.
Stokes starts his new spell with a short ball, Kohli initially looks to go for the pull but evades from the shot at the last moment as he sees the ball is way wide of the off stump.
Ends the over with yet another leave outside off.
Outside off again and Rahane leaves it again.
Woakes probing away on that line just outside off, Rahane chooses to let it go past.
Keeps it on the 6th stump line and Rahane shows respect. Shoulders arms.
Rahane will think he's missed out there. Again Woakes misses his line and length and bowls it short and wide. Rahane punches it to covers but cannot find the gap.

FOUR! SHOT! Short... Wide... Dispatched. Fifty for the vice-captain now. This is the best he has looked on this tour. Gets there in some style. A half-tracker outside off, Ajinkya stands tall and slashes it over point. The ball reaches to the fence in no time.
A little too wide outside off, Kohli need not play at those.
Bowls it on the stumps, Kohli pushes it to mid on.
On the middle stump, Kohli keeps it out.
Goes fuller in length on off, Kohli lunges and blocks it out.
Back of a length on off, Kohli shuffles across and blocks it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Well bowled by Woakes, he keeps it on a length just outside off. Rahane comes forward to defend it. But the ball gets a bit big on him and takes the outside edge. He does well though as he plays it with soft hands and this makes the ball drop in front of gully.
Plays this length ball around off with soft hands towards the point region. The batsmen run a single. Both looking well settled now.
Full on off, Kohli drives it well but straight to mid off.
Strays in line, on Rahane's pads who tucks it on the leg side for a single.
Rahane watchfully defends this length ball on the off stump into covers.

Fifty for the Indian captain, continues to grow in stature. A chanceless one too. Woakes starts a new spell with a back of a length ball outside off. Kohli reaches out for it, a bit away from his body and pushes this towards point for a single. He raises his bat to soak in all the applause by the crowd. He though will know best that the job is not done. He needs to carry on.
Chris Woakes comes back into the attack.
A little too wide outside off, the batsman shoulders his arms to it.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
Back to attacking the stumps, Rahane blocks it out.

FOUR! A little width on offer and Rahane pounces onto it. On the shorter side outside off, Rahane guides it through point. No fielder in the deep and the ball races away. Partnership into the 90s now.
Good length again on middle, not giving the batsman any room to free his hands. All Rahane can do is defend it onto the ground.
Length ball on off, Rahane defends it towards covers.
Floated outside off, tempting Kohli into the square drive, he gets it wide of the fielder at deep cover, they come back for two.
A bit shorter and spinning away, Kohli goes on the back foot and defends this rising delivery to keep it down.
Tossed up this time outside off, but Kohli has nothing to do with it.
FOUR! A gift from Rashid! And Kohli accepts it gleefully. Misses his line and length as he drags this one way down leg. Kohli pulls it easily to the deep square leg boundary for a boundary.
The runs are coming thick and fast, Rahane drill this tossed up delivery to the deep cover fielder for a single.
Slower and tossed up outside off, pulls his length back a bit, Kohli gets forward and pushes it cautiously to covers.
Bends his back on this one and bowls it on off, Rahane defends it onto the ground.
Excellent line by the great Anderson! Continuously attacking the off pole and landing it on a length. Rahane blocks it out.
Back of a length on off, Rahane opens the face of the bat and guides it to point.
Goes wide of the crease and angles it on off, Rahane gets behind the line and defends it onto the ground.
Good length around off, the batsman lunges and blocks it.
Bowls it on the pads, Kohli tucks it to fine leg and jogs to the other end.
A tighter over by Rashid comes to an end. Rahane is happy to let this flighted leg spinner go to Jonny.
Tossed up on the off stump. Rahane is happy to prod forward and keep it down.
Flighted leg spinner outside off. Rahane lets it go.
Rashid keeps it straighter and tosses this one a bit. Rahane keeps this out with soft hands.
Misfield again, shorter ball outside off, it is punched towards covers. The fielder there misfields and the ball is stopped by the fielder near the boundary line. The batsmen take two.
Rashid not afraid to toss it up, pitches it outside off, Kohli drills it to sweeper cover for a single. That man in the deep is a busy man as a lot of balls have been hit to him.
Maiden! Goes a touch fuller this time but does not get the swing he was looking for. Rahane pushes it to mid on.
Excellent stuff! Hits the same region for the 5th ball in a row. All Rahane can do is block it out.
4 in a row! Excellent Test match bowling. Anderson bowls it in the fifth stump channel. Rahane defends it towards covers.
Good length around off again, Rahane guides it towards point. Three good balls and three dots. Need to continue bowling there.
Good length again on off, Rahane is solid in defense like he has been throughout his innings.
On the stumps and on a good length. Rahane defends it.
You miss your length by a fraction and the Indian skipper will punish you. Kohli goes back to a shorter delivery on middle, whips it to deep square leg and gets two for it.
Flighted ball around off, Kohli drives this hard to covers. The crowd though lets out a huge roar as they feel it was a catch but it was a bump ball.
The googly is out! Rashid bowls it a bit quicker on off, Kohli goes back and pushes it to covers.
Kohli blocks this full length ball on the off stump.
Tossed up delivery on the off stump. Kohli defends off the front foot.
Rashid leaking runs here. Tossed up very full outside off and Rahane drives it sweetly to the man at sweeper cover for a single.

Howzzat? Not out is the answer to that question. Once again Kohli's stance and the way he has been playing came to his rescue. This is bowled outside off and it comes back in. Kohli lunges forward, planting his front foot outside the line of off. The ball beats his bat and hits the pads. The players appeal but the umpire shakes his head. The impact is an issue. But a testing over by Anderson nonetheless.
OHHHH! Very good leave! Anderson goes wide of the crease and angles it into the batsman. Kohli lets it be and it goes agonizingly close past the off pole.
FOUR! Too easy! Batting seems to be relatively easy now. No seam movement, no zip off the wicket. Anderson lands it outside off, Kohli leans into it and drives it through point for a boundary.
On middle, Kohli plants his front foot forward and works it to mid-wicket.
Good length on middle, kept out.
Huge shot but not given! On off, tailing back in. Kohli tries to drive but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Good ball to end the over. Tossed up on the off stump, Rahane prods forward and defends it into the ground.
Tighter line this time and fuller. Rahane gets right behind and blocks it down.
The bowler overcompensates and bowls it wide and short on off. Rahane gets the cut out for a couple of runs towards the deep point region.
Rashid goes shorter on Rahane's pads. AR rocks back and whips it towards the deep square leg boundary. The fielder there chases it down and they run two.
Fuller tossed up delivery outside off this time, Kohli drives it to the sweeper cover fielder for a run.
Rashid starts with a probing line outside. Kohli leaves it alone.

Drinks! An excellent hour of play for India. The skipper and the vice-captain have risen to the occasion, and have batted India out of the initial trouble. However, England will know the fact that a wicket or two here can turn the tide in their favor. What is in store after the break? Will India motor along or will England fight back? A gripping hour of play coming up!
A dot to end! On a length around off, AR blocks it.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Slightly straighter this time, Rahane nudges it around the corner and takes two.
Good length on off, Rahane this time gets behind the line and defends it out.
Excellent follow-up delivery. On a length and around off, this one pitches and moves away. Rahane plays inside the line and gets beaten.
FOUR! Runs flowing now! On the pads, Rahane is too good a batsman to miss out there. He flicks it through square leg and another boundary results. Back-to-back for India.

FOUR! Ends the over in style! Another excellent one for India. Another poor delivery by Rashid. A half-volley outside off, too full and hence the spin is out of contention. Kohli leans and strokes it through covers for the second boundary of the over.
Loopy ball outside off, left alone.
FOUR! A poor ball and it has been put away! Short and down the leg side, Kohli pulls it hard through backward square leg and there is no stopping that.
Again on the shorter side, the ball though is bowled quicker and Kohli pushes it to mid on.

On the shorter side, Kohli goes back and whips it through mid-wicket. He runs the first one hard and calls for the second. They complete it with ease and also brings the 50-run stand up. An important one for the visitors. The two joined when their team was in trouble, and now have steadied the ship. The job though is not done yet. They need to carry on.
Tosses it up on off, Kohli defends it onto the ground.
Adil Rashid is into the attack. Not to forget, he did not even bowl a single over in the last game. He would be eager to make an impact here.
On the middle stump, Rahane tucks it to mid-wicket.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
Just ahead of a length on middle, Rahane is solid in defense.
Hits the length around off, Rahane off the back foot blocks it.
Wide outside off, Rahane leaves it.
Back of a length delivery on off, this one shapes away a touch. Rahane goes back and tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
FOUR! This makes it even better. 11 from it. A freebie, a full toss on middle. It still has to be put away and Kohli ensures that. He flicks it through mid-wicket and there is no stopping after that.
Goes wide of the crease and angles this on the pads. Rahane nudges it towards square leg and gets to the other end. Good over this so far for India.
On the stumps and Rahane plays it with a straight bat to mid on. Good by the vice-captain, looking to score on the bad balls and respecting the good ones.
On the shorter side outside off, Kohli shuffles across and plays it through point for a run.
Make that 26 as he pushes it through covers and takes one.

FOUR! Good shot but a risky one! Not sure whether it is advisable to play so away from the body. On the shorter side outside off, Rahane guides it away from his body, through backward point for a boundary. He has quickly moved onto 25.
A touch short and outside off, Kohli goes on the back foot and defends it to the off side.
Soft hands again. A cautious attempt by the Indian batsmen today to do so. A delivery in the channel outside off, Kohli this time guides it down to third man and collects a couple of runs.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Outside off, tapped down from the back foot to point.

Lovely shot! Anderson pitches it up and outside off, moving away again. Rahane takes a big stride forward and just pushes it with good timing through extra cover. Root chases it down near the fence and they take three runs.
Starts with an outswinger outside off, on a fuller length, Rahane leaves it.
James Anderson is back.
Bowls this one in the channel outside off, a watchful leave to complete the over.
With a couple of fielders in the deep on the leg side, Stokes bowls it very full outside off. Double bluff by him. The Indian skipper reaches out for the delivery and squeezes it out to covers.
Stokes gets a length ball to move back into the batsman, Rahane works it off the inner half of the bat to fine leg for a single.

EDGY FOUR! Got out in a similar fashion in the last Test. It's short and outside off, shaping away. Rahane, with the temptation to hang his bat out, gets an outside edge which speeds past the third slip fielder (standing a few steps ahead than the normal position) for a boundary.
A good length ball outside off, Rahane gets forward and back before tapping it down towards point.
Stokes is brought back into the attack and he bowls a bouncer first up. It's outside off and an easy leave for Rahane.
That stays a touch low! But nothing to worry about as it was not on the stumps. Outside off, Kohli makes a leave.
Good length outside off, Virat shoulders arms to it.
Fuller in length on middle, trying to hit the pads of Kohli. The Indian skipper though is up to the task as he works it to mid-wicket.
Goes wide of the crease and angles this one into the batsman. Kohli tucks it with the angle to mid-wicket.
Hint of movement there. On a length and around off, shapes away. Kohli makes a leave.

FOUR! Exquisite! A half-volley on off, Kohli leans into it and strokes it through covers for a boundary. Once again no swing visible and hence it was bread and butter stuff for Virat. Partnership now moves onto 27.
On the stumps and blocked. Maiden over, not a threatening one though.
Well bowled! Closer to the off pole and gets this one to take off after pitching. Rahane does well to take his hands out of the way and let it go through to the keeper.
Full and wide outside off, wanting Rahane to go for the drive. Ajinkya resists and makes a leave.
Another slower ball on a fuller length. Rahane pushes it to mid off. Not a lot of movement on offer now, maybe because the sun is out. Good time for batting.
The cutter on off, Rahane goes back and defends it.
Wide outside off, Rahane lets it be.

This time a loud shout for an LBW but the umpire is unmoved. On the middle stump. Kohli tries to work it across the line but misses to get hit just above the knee roll. The players appeal but the umpire shakes his head. A little too high and Hawk Eye confirms that.
Another appeal but no reaction from the umpire. On the pads, Rahane fails to put bat to it. It hits his thigh pad and goes down to fine leg as the batsmen run a leg bye.

FOUR! Full marks to the bowler but runs to the batsman. Excellent delivery. He starts it on middle and gets it to shape away late. Rahane goes for the flick and he closes the face of his bat early. It takes the leading edge and goes through backward point for a boundary.
100 up for India, courtesy a leg bye! On the pads, Kohli tries to flick but misses. The ball brushes the pads and goes down to fine leg. The batsmen cross ends.
A little too wide outside off to make the batsman play.
A muted appeal! On a length around middle, Kohli misses the flick and gets high on the pads. The players start appealing but then bail out of it.
Lands it on off and on a good length. Rahane blocks it out.
Seeing there is not a lot of movement now. Broad hits the deck hard. Rahane hops and defends it onto the ground.
On middle, Kohli shuffles across and works it through mid-wicket. He gets a single, moves onto 12.
Shorter in length on off, Virat goes back and defends it out.
Back of a length this time on off, Kohli defends it off the back foot.

EDGED BUT SHORT! Good length and around off, this one pitches and straightens. Kohli tries to keep it out but gets an outside edge towards the man at third slip. We have seen this a lot of times in this series, the edges of Kohli's bat have not carried. Reason - he has been playing with soft hands.
Woakes goes for the magic delivery, trying to swing it from leg to off but the ball goes straight on. Kohli tucks it to fine leg for a run.
Goes fuller this time on off, no swing on offer. Kohli strokes it to mid off. Lets out a grunt after finding the fielder. He might have felt he missed out on a boundary.
Misfield! Slightly straighter this time by Woakes. Rahane clips it towards mid-wicket. Anderson there misfields and concedes three extra runs. Runs now have started to come for India.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! Nicely timed! Woakes pays the price of bowling it very full. Rahane just leans into the stroke and times it through mid off. The ball races away to the fence.
Good amount of movement again but the line is outside off, Rahane makes a leave.
Good length again on off, this one takes off after pitching. Kohli tries to block but gets an outside edge towards gully.
Runs again! Broad strays in line and bowls it on the pads, Kohli loves it there, he flicks it through mid-wicket and the batsmen run two.
Down the leg side, Kohli misses out and Jonny behind does well to collect it diving to his left.
Fullish outside off, Kohli guides it through backward point and takes two. He opened the face of the bat at the very last moment which saw the ball going wide of Stokes at point.
Excellent stop! Full and outside off, Kohli leans into it and drives it towards point. Stokes there dives to his left and saves a few runs for his side.
That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads.
Another delivery outside off, Rahane does not play at it.
Goes back to bowling it on off, Rahane stands tall and guides it to point.
Off the mark with a brace! A rare loose delivery by Woakes. On the pads, Rahane is quite strong through the leg side, he flicks it through square leg and runs two.
Fuller in length again outside off, Rahane need not play at those.
Slightly fuller and on off, shapes away a touch. Rahane prods forward and strokes it to covers.
On a length and around off, Rahane keeps it out.

Ends an excellent over with another beauty! Once again the corridor of uncertainty. Kohli is not sure whether to play at it or leave it. He tries to pull his bat out at the very last moment but the ball hits the bottom half and then Kohli's body. A round of applause as Broad takes his hat from the umpire and he deserves every bit of it.
Pitches it in a similar area as the last one but this time it goes straight on. Kohli keeps it out.

PEACH! You can just hope deliveries such as these miss the outside edge. Lovely, lovely stuff. He goes wide of the crease and then angles it into the batsman. Kohli has to play at it due to the original trajectory. The ball pitches and the leaves him, beating the outside edge.

Nicely played for the first runs after the break! Back of a length delivery outside off, Kohli waits for the delivery and plays it late. He opens the face of his bat and guides it through short third man for a couple.
Attacks the stumps and bowls it just behind a length. Kohli once again is solid in defense.
He too starts perfectly! On a length and around off, no swing on offer for him on this delivery. Kohli lunges and blocks it.
Stuart Broad will continue from the other end.
Goes fuller this time in search of some swing and does get it. He shapes it appreciably away from the batter. Rahane watchfully lets it be. End of a wicket-maiden.
Right on the money after the break. Hits the length hard and pitches it on off, Rahane gets behind the line of the delivery and defends it.
We are back for the afternoon session. Out come the batsmen, Virat Kohli and Ajinkya Rahane who is the new man in. Chris Woakes will continue his over. Here we go...
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

The home team started in a bit of a frantic fashion after putting the visitors into bat. Anderson and Broad bowled good lines and lengths but they were inconsistent with it. This allowed the Indian openers to get into the game and put a 50-run stand, first for the opening wicket since Edgbaston. Once Woakes and Stokes got the ball in their hand, they started pushing the pressure back on the opposition batters. Their consistency earned England wickets of the opening duo, and just before the Lunch break, they managed to remove Pujara as well. The number 1 Test team is in the usual territory, reeling behind in the game. The post-lunch session starts in a while, hang around.

How the fortunes change, I dare say. India, who were cruising before the drinks break, have now lost their third wicket just at the stroke of lunch. This has an uncanny resemblance to the first innings of the first Test where they were reduced to 76/3 after getting a similar start. Pujara's reckless shot cost him his wicket, which now has put the visitors' fragile middle-order in for a test. It was India's session up until drinks as I said, losing no wickets. Both Rahul and Dhawan started well, showed intent while leaving and defending, and when they got the loose balls, they made sure they capitalized on it. Woakes, the star of the Lord's game, put his hand up yet again, and has got his side right back in the contest.

OUT! What? How could you Pujara, how could you, and that too on the cusp of Lunch? It was a nothing delivery, a short ball on middle and leg. He pulls it with power. If only he had hit it 10 meters left or right to Rashid at fine leg, it would have gone for a boundary but no. Rashid only has to take a few steps across to his left to pouch an easy catch. Pujara is shell-shocked, so is Ravi Shastri in the dressing room, and Kohli looks bamboozled as well. On the other hand, Woakes can't believe his luck as he celebrates with a huge smile on his face. Pujara keeps on finding unusual ways to get out. Anyhow, that's LUNCH ON DAY 1.
On middle and off, worked to mid-wicket for nothing.
Outside off, left alone.
Pujara hangs back and gets it to the on side.
Fuller and wider of off, this time Kohli goes for the drive, gets the middle of the bat but is hit straight to the man at point.
just ahead of a length on off, ball seams back in and Kohli taps this nicely towards the mid-wicket region.
Leaves this full out-swinging delivery alone.
back of a length delivery on middle, pitches and jags back in. Kohli looks to tuck this into the on side but the movement beats his bat and is struck on his thigh-pad.
Length ball outside off, Kohli watches it like a hawk and lets it go past him.

Broad bowls it full on off stump, it's swinging in as Kohli looks to defend, is beaten by the swing and the ball hits his front pad. England appeal loud and hard but the Umpire is unmoved. England players discuss and then go for the review. Replay shows it's impact outside off stump and that's enough for the Indian captain to continue.
Review time! Broad has convinced his skipper to take the review for an LBW. Virat Kohli is the man in question. It looks to have hit him outside the line of the stumps though.
Length again outside off, Pujara allows it through.
Continues with the same line and length but cannot break Pujara's patience, he keeps on leaving them.
Fuller outside off, lets it go to Bairstow.
Length ball on off, Pujara shoulders arms.
Straighter on length from Woakes and Kohli brings out his flick. Finds the gap at mid-wicket and times it well enough for the batsmen to cross over for three.
Fuller but outside off. Left alone by Kohli.
WOW! How did that miss the stumps? Length ball on off, Pujara prods forward to defend but the ball nips back into him and cuts him into half. That was a peach from Broad.
Length ball on the stumps, defended off the back foot.
Pujara looking confident as he punches this back of a length ball outside off, past the point fielder. They take two.
Length ball angling in on middle, Kohli works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Length ball on stumps, Kohli defends it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Beaten! Tentative from Kohli. Broad bowls this on a length just outside off. Kohli looks to get bat on ball. But the ball pitches and seams away to beat Virat's tentative poke.
He has nothing to do with this length ball on off, lets it go past.
Lands it on a length ball outside off, left alone by Pujara.
Length ball on off, Pujara stays back and taps it with soft hands towards the gully region.

FOUR! That's bread and butter for Pujara. He will play this shot even in his sleep. Fuller and just outside off. Pujara gets forward and times his cover drive well enough for the ball to cross over the boundary easily. Pujara is off to a brisk start.
Length ball again, wide outside off, left alone again by the batsman.
Length ball outside off, left alone by Pujara.

The Pujara square drive, so pleasing to the eyes. He leans forward to this very full ball outside off and elegantly times the drive through the cover-point region. The batsmen cross over for three runs.
Too wide to tempt Pujara into a shot. Left alone.

Four byes! Big booming in-swinger again, but the swing is just too much this time. The ball misses Pujara's pads and also the diving keeper. Four runs gifted to India who will take it with both hands open.
This one comes in. A bit fuller on on off, Pujara looks to defend but the inswing takes the inner half of the bat and the ball rolls in front of square leg.
Length ball outside off, left alone by Pujara.
Short of a length ball on off, Pujara goes on the back foot and taps it down.
Skipper Virat Kohli is the new batsman walking in.

OUT! That's gone, hitting leg. KL continues with his walk to the pavilion. Woakes has removed both the openers. He delivers a length ball on off stump, it pitches and nips back in sharply to beat Rahul who was trying to defend. Then, it sneaks past the inner edge of the bat and traps him on the pads. The appeal follows and umpire Erasmus has given him out. The Indian opener starts to walk but Pujara calls him and suggests to go for the DRS. Rahul, who was seen saying 'no bat', decides to take the review. The replays roll in and they show three reds. Rahul's fight ends and India lose a review as well.

KL Rahul has been trapped in front. Up goes the finger after the appeal is made and the Indian opener starts to walk. Pujara calls him back and suggests to take the DRS. Rahul is seen saying 'no bat' but Che still wants him to take the help of the technology. Here we go then. To us, that looks to be out. Let's see...
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Rahul is not tempted to play this wide and full ball swinging away.
Beaten! Shorter of a length on off this time, Rahul tries to play at it but the away movement after pitching beats the outside edge. Rahul is safe.
Rahul chooses to leave this length ball outside off, moving away.
Length ball on the stumps, it's defended from within the crease.
Length ball outside off, left alone.

Big booming inswinger this time from Stokes. Goes wide of the crease and fires a full ball on middle, swings in but Pujara is up to the mark. He watches it till the end and tucks it onto the on side, albeit off the inside edge.
Shorter of a length on off, Pujara stands tall and blocks it.

FOUR! Stokes goes wide of the crease and angles it back in from the off stump. Pujara has worked it off his pads behind square. The ball races to the boundary. Four runs has been signalled by the umpire
Too wide to tempt the batsman. Shorter and wider of off stump. Pujara lets it go past him.
Starts the over with a length ball outside off, Pujara watches it carefully and lets it go past to Bairstow.
And Cheteshwar Pujara is off the mark. A fuller ball on off, swinging away, Pujara leans forward and pushes this softly towards covers, both batsmen take a quick single.
Length ball on off, Pujara taps it towards point with soft hands. No run.
Cheteshwar Pujara is the next batsman in.

OUT! Excellent delivery and India's first wicket goes down. It's that man Woakes again who tormented India at Lord's. Bowls this just short of a length on and around the off stump line. The ball pitches and nips away. Dhawan tries to defend it with a straight bat, but the movement is just enough to take the outside edge as he gets squared up. It flies to second slip where Buttler makes no error. England draw first blood after toiling hard for over an hour.
Closer to the batsman this time but wide enough for Dhawan to leave it alone.
Lets this fuller and wider ball outside off go behind
Length ball outside off, Dhawan has nothing to do with it, left alone.

WOW! An absolute jaffa this from Stokes. He bowls this from wide of the crease, going further in to KL. The ball first swings in the air, lands outside off and then curls back in sharply. It goes past the hanging bat of Rahul who is beaten all ends up.
FOUR! Intentional or not? Does not matter I'd say. A half-tracker just outside off, Rahul goes hard at it and gets an outside edge perhaps. It goes over the slip cordon and into the fence.
Outside off, left alone.
On middle and off, defended.
Rahul lets the ball go outside his off stump.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Good shot for no runs. Short of a length ball outside off, Dhawan rocks back and cuts it fiercely but straight to the man at point. Both batsmen looking good though.
On a length outside off, left alone by Dhawan.
Length ball on off, pitches and nips back in. Rahul tucks it into the leg side for a quick single.
Outside off, left alone by Rahul.

FOUR! Well played by Rahul. Length ball on off, pitches and nips away but Rahul has taken the movement into account. He prods forward and tries to defend it with gentle hands. The ball takes the outer half and races past third slip to the boundary.

FOUR! Cracker from Rahul, one of the best of the innings, so far. Woakes bowls this full and just outside off, swinging away. Rahul leans forward and gets out a superbly timed cover drive. Races away through the vacant region. Rahul looking good. That's the 50 of the partnership, first for the opening wicket since Edgbaston's 1st innings.
The ball is down the leg side but Dhawan still goes after it and misses.
Fuller on off, punched to mid off for no run.
FOUR! Short and wide and crashed through cover-point again. Relentless Dhawan punishing everything through the off side.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.

Pheeww! Dhawan had his heart in his mouth for a moment there. A back of a length, pitching on off, moving away from the batsman. He pokes at it with a straight bat only to get an outside edge. Luckily for him the ball lands just in front of the fielder at third slip.
Outside off, left alone.

Drinks have been called by the umpires. A much-needed cup of coffee in this chilly Nottingham morning. For the visitors, their team will be feeling relaxed considering they have not lost a wicket. England have not done too badly either but they have been a bit wayward with their lines, to be honest.
Last ball before the drinks break. Rahul shoulders his arms to the ball outside off. End of a good first hour for India.
Gets beaten! Rahul looks to cut the length ball outside off and misses it.
A touch too straight this time on the pads, Dhawan flicks it behind square leg for a run.
Similar delivery from Chris and Shikhar keeps his bat away from the line.
Woakes at it again, right where he left in the last game. A back of a length ball moving away from the Dhawan who fails to put bat to ball.
Woakes bowls a shortish ball first up. Dhawan blocks it.
Chris Woakes is on.
Nothing to do with the ball outside off again.
In that same channel outside where KL has been more than willing to leave the ball.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Jeez! Stokes is keeping SD in check. A length ball jagging back in prodigiously. Dhawan gets the inner half of the bat to fine leg for a run. Had he missed that, it could have been tight.
Just outside off, cut to point.
Around off, Dhawan comes forward and manages to keep it away from his pads.
Brilliant again. A leave to the ball outside off. You need to put your heart and mind into your batting to survive Anderson's bowling. This pair has done that efficiently till now.
Rahul showing some good temperament here. He is adamant not to play the wide deliveries outside off. He lets another one through.
Similar stuff from the bowler and the batsman.
Outside off, left alone.
Some width on this one as Rahul gets into the position quickly to cut but couldn't get it past the gully fielder.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Good stuff from Stokes as well as Rahul. A back of a length ball coming in with the angle. KL manages to defend it adjacent to the pitch on the on side. A quick run stolen. Excellent stuff from this duo. They have been proactive in their approach.
Comes forward and works this one to mid off. One run taken.
The batsman shoulders arms to let this one through.
Keeps his bat away from the line of the ball and lets it be.
FOUR! Short, wide and punished. Dhawan hasn't let any opportunity to score go past him. He crunches this one through covers and finds the gap.
A length ball coming in to the left-hander who lets it be for the keeper by keeping his bat behind his pad.
KL lets the ball go outside his off stump. A testing over from James.
Hangs back to play this one through covers. A run results.
Wowza! Anderson is asking some difficult questions now. An in-swinger on middle and off, Dhawan gets it to the short square leg fielder off the inner half of the bat.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.

Was that intentional? I don't think so. James brings one in to SD who looks to get his bat away from the line but the ball goes off the outside edge towards the slip cordon. Soft hands and playing it late helped him there.
Back of a length ball from around the wicket on off. Dhawan defends it.
Excellent stuff from the duo. This time Dhawan uses the soft hands and taps the ball to the off side for another quick single.
Plays the length ball with soft hands to point and gets to the other end easily. Good start this from India.
Gets on his toes to keep the back of a length ball away.
On the leg stump line, Dhawan fails to put bat to ball as it hits his pads. A leg bye stolen.
FOUR! Thrashed! Dhawan gets some width on this angled length ball and he does not miss. He gets into position quickly and flashes hard to pierce the gap through the covers.
Ben starts the over with a shortish ball on middle and off, Rahul half-pulls it to deep mid-wicket and runs a single.
Ben Stokes is on as the first change.
Another easy leave outside off as the score moves to 26/0 after 9 overs.
On middle, on length, Rahul works it through mid-wicket and runs a single.
Rahul lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Shows the full face and blocks it.
Tentative Rahul does not fiddle with the wide ball.
Outside off, an easy leave for KL.

FOUR! Goodness me, that was close. Dhawan will take it. A length ball on off and coming into the batsman who is late on the shot after moving across a bit. The ball takes the inside half of the bat and another boundary through the fine leg region results.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

FOUR! Being a bowler myself, I can relate to what Broad wanted to do there, but it's not advisable to say the least. To move it further away from Dhawan, he bowls this one on middle and looks to swing it away from him, however, it wasn't to be. Dhawan easily clips the length which drops on his hips. A boundary through the vacant fine leg region.
Oohs and aahs all around the ground as Broad moves the ball like Beckham. A just short of a length ball, pitching just outside off and it moves away after pitching, beating Dhawan all ends up.
Too wide, SD has no interest in those.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Testing stuff from the talisman. Another beauty just outside off and beating the hanging bat of Rahul. No harm done in the end.
Easy-peasy for Rahul to let this one through outside off. He needs to be watchful of the one coming back into him.
On the fifth stump, Rahul ignores it.
Rahul shoulders arms to let that one through.
Right-hander's nightmare is this man, and here he shows why. Another angled ball, just a tad shorter than the previous one and moving away from KL after pitching. He fails to put bat to ball.
Fuller, coming in with the angle and then jagging away after pitching. KL lets it be.
Dhawan moves across and defends the back of a length ball to the on side for nothing. 5 runs in this over.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through after shuffling across.

Michael Holding and David Lloyd (on air) appear to be in a trolling mood this morning. First the West Indian displays his dry humour by saying that the Indian players are wearing black armbands and that's not because they are 0-2 down in the series. Then, he points to Root who was shining the ball and jokes that the best way to roughen up one side will be to use a sandpaper and Bumble also joins him in that. The former pacer quickly asks him, is he indicating towards a particular team? That's quite cheeky. Now, the camera pans to Adil Rashid and David quips what a Test match he had at Lord's. Haha!
Hangs back and keeps it out.
Dhawan lets the ball go outside his off stump.
KL shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot to the leg side. They pick up a single.

FOUR! Pure class and timing on this one. That's Rahul for you. A fullish ball closer to the off pole, Rahul prods forward and middles the ball nicely. It races through cover-point and Ben Stokes has no chance of stopping it.

FOUR! Up and over the slip cordon and it goes to the third man boundary. Dhawan flashes hard at the back of a length and as a result, it goes over off the outside edge. A good over for India nonetheless.
Outside off, worked to the off side for no run.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.

FOUR! And the pressure is released. A gentle loosener on the pads, Dhawan flicks and gets it through backward square leg for the first boundary of the morning. Anderson is looking off-colour, to be honest.
Another play and a miss from Dhawan. He goes after the widish ball and fails to connect.
On middle and leg, Rahul taps it to the off side and scampers for a run.

Jaffa! Dhawan is late on it. He didn't judge the line or the length of this one. A 'Broad-length' ball just outside off, it whizzes past the inside of Dhawan's bat. A cracker of an over from Broad, another maiden bowled by him.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
