Ooh! No, no, no, you can't do that here mate. This is England and the ball moves like a yo-yo here. Got to keep those hands closer to the body. Dhawan goes after a beauty of a delivery, on a length just outside off. Due to the angle Broad is creating from 'round the wicket, it lands and goes away from Dhawan who misses it.
Closer to the off pole, straightening just a tad. Dhawan taps it to the off side for nothing.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Too wide outside off, Dhawan lets it be.
Easy leave for Rahul. Anderson keeps it tight on the fifth stump line to end the over.
The ball hits Dhawan low on the pads and rolls towards short fine leg. One run stolen. The umpire signals a leg bye.
No prodigious movement for James as of now as Dhawan lefts the angled ball outside his off to the keeper.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Watchful Dhawan lets another one through outside his off stump.
Fullish, angled across Shikhar who lets it be outside his off stump.
Angling into the batsman from a length around off, Rahul defends it from the crease to end a pretty innocuous over.
Broad has still not hit the top pace. A gentle one in the corridor outside off, KL watches the line, covers his stumps and allows it through.

Oohhh...a play and a miss! This wasn't too far away from the outside edge. Once again the angle is around the off stump line, forcing the batsman on the front foot but the late away movement beats the outside edge of Rahul's bat who was looking to defend.
This time Broad brings a good length ball back into the batsman. It's more towards the off stump line and Rahul is forced to play at it. He does so from the back foot and blocks it down safely.
Another delivery which has been served in the zone outside off, Rahul is very cautious as he walks across a bit before leaving it unplayed.
Starts with a good length delivery in the channel outside off, not much evident movement, Rahul has a comfortable leave to make.
Stuart Broad to share the new ball from the other end. A pretty similar field for him too. Rahul on strike for the first time.
On a length angling away from the Shikhar who let's one through. So, a rather ordinary over considering the previous matches. No wicket this time. India rejoice!
Dhawan shoulders arms to let that one through.
Full and down the leg side. As per the theories, Anderson doesn't get it right to the left-handers straightaway. Dhawan looks to flick it but misses.
On a length around middle and off, blocked.
A touch too straight this time. Pitches on middle and goes towards leg. Dhawan flicks it through deep fine leg and takes a couple. First runs on the board for India and Dhawan.
Starts with a little bit of curve in the first ball. The ball lands on a length and comes back into Dhawan from off. Well defended.

Avada Kedavra! Boom-tish! With some black magical prayers to keep the rains away, we are all set for the third Test. Shikhar Dhawan and KL Rahul are out in the middle and are wearing black armbands to mourn the death of the former captain, Ajit Wadekar. James Anderson, as expected, has the new cherry in his hand. Four slips in place. Here we go...

India skipper, Virat Kohli says that they wanted to bat first. He believes there is grass on the pitch but it looks like a good batting track. Adds that the batsmen are looking to be positive and enter with a mindset to score runs. Expects the surface to slow down after a couple of days and reckons that the spinners may come into play later on in the match. Admits that this is a very important game for them but staying in the moment and being positive is what they will be focusing on. Informs about a few tactical as well as combination changes in the playing XI as Murali Vijay, Kuldeep Yadav and Dinesh Karthik make way for Shikhar Dhawan, Jasprit Bumrah and Rishabh Pant (on Test debut).

England skipper, Joe Root says he will bowl first as there is a lot of grass on the track and they'll look to make most of it. Further adds that they are bowling well right now and these are good conditions for their fast bowlers to exploit. Informs that Ben Stokes comes in for Sam Curran and reckons that Adil Rashid may come into play later on as the pitch gets drier. Asserts that they are excited as a team and would look to continue with the same momentum that they have carried until now. Ends by saying that they are elated to be in the position they are in, however, they still need to play their best in the next few days to stay on the winning side.
TOSS - England win the toss and elect to bowl.

Pitch Report - Sanjay Manjrekar says the weather possibilities (referring to rain) are less for the next 5 days. Further adds that the temperature has dropped and it feels cooler. Reckons the surface has a liberal covering of grass with green as well as brown sheen underneath the fresh crop. Expects it to be dry, and spinners would come into play from Day 3 onward. Adds that the seamers will enjoy bowling on this pitch, especially early on in the day. Ends by saying that the pitch may suit the Indian batsmen.

As the saying goes, the show must go on. We welcome you all and thank you for joining us for the third Test match between England and India at Trent Bridge, Nottingham. One team has a problem of plenty wherein the other team has a plenty of problem. The hosts are 2-0 ahead after demolishing the tourists at Lord�s and will be trying to seal the series here itself. On the other hand, India have their backs to the wall and appear to be struggling to get the right combination. Let's see how they go about their business in this game.

Let's begin by saying India are going through a lot, and I'm not talking about cricket. The country celebrated their 72nd Independence Day a few days back and since then, it's been news of tragedy after tragedy. First the news of Ajit Wadekar's demise plunged the cricketing world into mourning and the very next day, an iconic political leader and the former Prime Minister, Shree Atal Bihari Vajpayee breathed his last. Both leaving a lasting legacy. The country is trying to recover from these huge losses and now, the news of Kerala's woes came in where the unprecedented rain has brought the state to a standstill, claiming many lives. In these tough times, we pray for the situation to improve and get back to normalcy as soon as possible.
